audit_findings.title: Gross cash bridge may add operating and trapped cash at par
audit_findings.magnitude: $495.3 million, equal to $3.13 per share and 17.3% of base equity value; $116.6 million, or $0.74 per share, was held in Israel, Canada and China
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds all cash to equity at par after removing portfolio interest income from owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: Other than for Krausz’s investment in its United States subsidiary and other anticipated distributions which result cumulatively in immaterial income tax, we have not recorded income taxes for unrepatriated foreign earnings that may be subject to withholding tax or any outside cost basis differences inherent in our foreign subsidiaries, as these amounts continue to be indefinitely reinvested in foreign operations.
audit_findings.explanation: Adding the entire $495.3 million is demonstrated, but the record does not demonstrate that all of it is distributable excess cash. Foreign cash of $116.6 million is specifically identified, while minimum operating cash, legal restrictions and repatriation costs remain unresolved. The exposed bridge amount is large enough to materially affect every per-share scenario.
audit_findings.action: Determine restricted and minimum operating cash by jurisdiction, quantify repatriation costs, and rerun all scenarios using only demonstrably distributable excess cash.

audit_findings.title: Unaccrued environmental indemnity is an unmodeled senior claim
audit_findings.mechanism: A remediation payment would reduce future owner earnings or require a direct deduction from the equity bridge as a claim senior to common equity.
audit_findings.evidence: Since the amounts of such costs cannot be reasonably estimated at this time, no amounts have been accrued for this matter as of September 30, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The indemnity and absence of an accrual are demonstrated, but no remediation cost, allocation or recoverable amount can be estimated from the record. The latest 10-Q still reports no accrual and identifies three other PRPs. A value effect is possible, but materiality cannot presently be established.
audit_findings.action: Obtain current EPA cost estimates, PRP allocation and viability evidence, insurance or indemnity recoveries, and then rerun the bridge with a probability-weighted net liability.

audit_findings.title: Prospective capital spending exceeds the FY2025 run rate
audit_findings.magnitude: $12.7-$17.7 million annual increase over FY2025, equal to 8.0%-11.1% of the $158.9 million anchor OE; nine-month FY2026 capex was $43.6 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Required maintenance, compliance or growth-supporting capital spending reduces owner earnings and may also constrain the growth assumptions.
audit_findings.evidence: We estimate 2026 capital expenditures will be between $60.0 million and $65.0 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The higher spending plan and current increase are demonstrated: FY2026 guidance is $60-$65 million versus $47.3 million in FY2025, and nine-month spending rose by $10.8 million year over year. Whether the increment is recurring required capital or discretionary expansion remains unresolved, but the possible annual deduction is material relative to anchor OE.
audit_findings.action: Classify the FY2026 program into maintenance, compliance and discretionary growth capital, then rerun owner earnings and all scenarios with the recurring required portion deducted.

audit_findings.title: Tariff pressure may invalidate margin-based growth assumptions
audit_findings.magnitude: approximately $27.4 million gross annual exposure using 3% of FY2025 cost of sales of $913.0 million; net OE effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Unrecovered tariff costs reduce margins and owner earnings; price increases used to recover dollars may also affect volume and sustainable growth.
audit_findings.evidence: In addition, higher direct tariff costs of approximately 3% of costs of goods sold are expected to continue to contribute to inflationary pressures in 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: This is not merely hypothetical: the latest 10-Q says Section 232 tariffs are already creating material cost pressure and negatively affected nine-month results, although pricing and nonrecurring refunds provided offsets. The gross exposure equals 17.2% of anchor OE, so even partial non-recovery can materially affect value. The precise net effect remains unresolved because realized pricing, volume effects and refunds are not separately quantified.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild normalized OE from FY2026 results, remove nonrecurring tariff refunds, quantify realized price-cost recovery by segment, and rerun the 0%, 4% and 7% growth cases.

audit_findings.title: Customer concentration creates a discontinuity not represented by smooth growth rates
audit_findings.magnitude: 37% of FY2025 gross sales; $98.9 million of receivables from the two customers at September 30, 2025
audit_findings.mechanism: Loss or repricing of a major distributor would cause a step-down in revenue, margins and owner earnings that smooth growth rates do not explicitly represent.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company has two significant customers that comprise greater than 10% of gross sales.
audit_findings.explanation: Concentration is demonstrated: the customers represented 20% and 17% of FY2025 gross sales and $56.5 million and $42.4 million of receivables. No customer loss, repricing event or deterioration is established, so this remains a forward-looking discontinuity risk rather than a present valuation error.
audit_findings.action: Monitor purchasing and receivable trends, obtain contract and switching-risk evidence, and add explicit loss or margin-repricing sensitivities if either relationship weakens.

audit_findings.title: NMTC recapture guarantee is outside ordinary debt treatment
audit_findings.mechanism: A compliance failure could create a one-time cash claim against equity that is not represented by ordinary debt principal or recurring owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: Wells Fargo is entitled to the associated tax credits, which are subject to 100% recapture if we do not comply with various regulations and contractual provisions surrounding the foundry project.
audit_findings.explanation: The indemnity and 100% recapture condition are demonstrated, but no breach or expected recapture is reported. Management continues to expect a nominal December 2027 settlement and an estimated $3.9 million gain. The maximum indemnification exposure is not disclosed, so the contingent loss cannot be assessed for present materiality.
audit_findings.action: Confirm continuing NMTC compliance, obtain the tax-credit recapture schedule and maximum indemnity, verify the recorded liability, and deduct a probability-weighted claim only if compliance evidence deteriorates.
